theme: refusals: what makes him NOT trade (neither / no / none / X)

claims.rule: No level to break-and-retest against is a standalone refusal reason, distinct from a level being present but not respected (chop). When he cannot find any PDH/PDL/PMH/PML/pivot/OR/HOD/LOD to reference, he refuses the trade outright, even on otherwise-clean price action. Contradiction to note: he does NOT refuse a clean setup just because it lacks a level to TARGET for profit (QQQ_2025-08-01 graded S with the same complaint) -- the refusal is specific to no level to enter/retest against, not no level to exit at.

claims.predicate_sketch: Not ratified/wired as a distinct rule in omen-rulebook.md -- the rulebook's level_not_respected (CHOP_TOUCHES=2) covers a level that exists but is being chopped through, not the absence of any level at all. This is a different failure mode (no candidate level in the lookback window) and should be measured separately before wiring; the QQQ_2025-08-01 counterexample (no level to TARGET, still S) means any implementation must distinguish entry-level absence from target-level absence.
